Implement the following change to the application so that it fully satisfies the
specification and all existing and new tests pass.

As you do, keep the code well structured: put each piece of logic where it belongs, in a
small unit with a single responsibility, and reuse existing code instead of copying it. Do
not let any one class or method grow into a catch-all that accumulates unrelated logic. Run
the test suite and make it green before finishing.

The locality derivation must now prefer the postcode: look up the region by postcode range first (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099), and only fall back to the city-to-region table when the postcode is absent or in no known range. This returns the same region for known cities but disambiguates cities that share a name.

probe.probe_text:
Here is the complete, ordered sequence of what happens when an owner is created via `POST /api/owners`, handled by `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner` (`src/main/java/.../rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java:143-171`).

## Before the method body

0. **Authorization** — `@PreAuthorize("hasRole(@roles.OWNER_ADMIN)")` requires the `OWNER_ADMIN` role. (Bean Validation on `OwnerFieldsDto` — e.g. `@Size`, the 4-digit postcode pattern — is also applied by Spring on binding, before the handler runs.)

## In `addOwner`, in order

1. **Normalize address** (side-effect, on the DTO) — `AddressNormalizer.normalize(...)`: trims, collapses internal whitespace, upper-cases, and expands whole-word street abbreviations (`ST→STREET`, `RD→ROAD`, `AVE→AVENUE`). `null` stays `null`.

2. **Validate required fields** — `OwnerFieldsValidator.validateRequiredFields(...)`: rejects if any of `firstName`, `lastName`, `address`, `city`, `telephone` is null or blank → `MissingOwnerFieldsException`. (Runs on the already-normalized address.)

3. **Map DTO → `Owner`** entity (`ownerMapper.toOwner`).

4. **Normalize + validate telephone** (side-effect) — `TelephoneNormalizer.normalize(...)`: strips formatting, produces canonical E.164 (`+` then 8–15 digits), defaulting to `+61` and dropping a leading `0` when no country code is given. Rejects a wrong total length, or a national-number length that doesn't match a recognized country → `InvalidTelephoneException`.

5. **Normalize + validate email** (side-effect) — `EmailNormalizer.normalize(...)`: lower-cases; if present it must match the email regex → `InvalidEmailException`. `null` (email is optional) stays `null`.

6. **Validate postcode** — `PostcodeValidator.validate(city, postcode)`: if a postcode is present, it must fall in the range for the city's region → `InvalidPostcodeException`. `null` postcode is accepted; unknown region accepts any 4-digit value.

7. **Set registration date** (side-effect) — defaults to `LocalDate.now()` if none was supplied, then rolls it forward to a business day via `BusinessDayAdjuster.toBusinessDay(...)` (Sat/Sun → next Monday).

8. **Daily capacity check** — `dailyRegistrationCapacityValidator.validateHasCapacity(registrationDate)`: rejects if ≥ 100 owners already registered on that (business) day → `DailyRegistrationLimitExceededException`.

9. **Household assignment** (conditional side-effect) — only if `sharesHousehold` is `TRUE`: `householdRegistrar.assignHousehold(owner)`. If an existing household (same last name + address) is found, it shares/derives one `householdId` and **saves the existing members** that lacked it, then sets the new owner's `householdId`. If no such household exists, nothing is assigned.

10. **Identity uniqueness check** — `identityUniquenessValidator.validateUnique(owner)`: rejects if any existing owner has the same identity key (`normalizedTelephone + '|' + email + '|' + householdId`) → `DuplicateOwnerIdentityException`. (Runs after telephone/email/household are in final form.)

11. **City capacity check** — `cityOwnerCapacityValidator.validateHasCapacity(city)`: rejects if the city (case-insensitive) already holds ≥ 50 owners → `CityOwnerCapacityExceededException`.

12. **Set namesake count** (side-effect) — `namesakeCounter.count(firstName, lastName)`: number of existing owners with the same first+last name (case-insensitive), stored on the owner.

13. **Generate customer code** (side-effect) — `CustomerCodeGenerator.generate(city, lastName, cityOwnerCounter.count(city))`: `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>`, where NNNN = (current case-insensitive city owner count) + 1, zero-padded.

14. **Persist the owner** — `clinicService.saveOwner(owner)` (assigns the id).

15. **Generate membership number** (side-effect, post-save) — `MembershipNumberGenerator.generate(customerCode, registrationDate)`: `<customerCode>-M<YY>` using the last two digits of the registration year.

16. **Audit log** (side-effect) — `ownerAuditLogger.logCreated(owner)`: writes one line to the `AUDIT` logger with id, customer code, registration date, and membership level.

17. **Build response** — map to `OwnerDto`, set the `Location` header to `/api/owners/{id}`, and return `201 CREATED`.

A couple of things worth noting: the method is **not `@Transactional`**, so the existing-member saves in step 9 and the new-owner save in step 14 are separate commits — a rejection in steps 10/11 after a household backfill in step 9 leaves those backfill saves persisted. Also `membershipNumber` (step 15) is set only on the in-memory entity *after* the save, so it's returned in the response but is not itself persisted by this handler.
